quickSummary: Dipole moment (μ = q × d) measures bond polarity. Symmetrical molecules have μ_net = 0. In NH₃ vs NF₃, NH₃ has a higher dipole moment (1.47 D vs 0.23 D) because N-H bond dipoles reinforce the lone pair dipole vector.
summary: Master dipole moment calculations, vector summation in polyatomic shapes, the NH₃ vs NF₃ paradox, and percentage ionic character.

summaryBox.title: Dipole Moment

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DIPOLE MOMENT VECTOR (μ)
                         
   μ = q × d
   
   ├── Units: Debye (D) ⟹ 1 D = 3.33564 × 10⁻³⁰ C·m = 10⁻¹⁸ esu·cm
   └── Direction: Vector points from Electropositive (δ+) to Electronegative (δ-).
conceptBreakdown.content:
For polyatomic molecules, the net dipole moment ($\mu_{\text{net}}$) is the vector sum of bond dipoles and lone-pair dipoles:

$$\mathbf{\mu_{\text{net}} = \sqrt{\mu_1^2 + \mu_2^2 + 2\mu_1\mu_2 \cos\theta}}$$

• **Symmetric Cancellation**:
- $\text{CO}_2$ (Linear, $180^\circ$): $\text{O} \leftarrow \text{C} \rightarrow \text{O} \implies \mathbf{\mu_{\text{net}} = 0}$
- $\text{BF}_3$ (Trigonal Planar, $120^\circ$): Vectors cancel completely $\implies \mathbf{\mu_{\text{net}} = 0}$
- $\text{CCl}_4$ (Tetrahedral, $109.5^\circ$): Vectors cancel completely $\implies \mathbf{\mu_{\text{net}} = 0}$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 The NH3 vs NF3 Dipole Paradox
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 The NH3 vs NF3 Dipole Paradox
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
NH₃ vs NF₃ DIPOLE MOMENT COMPARISON
                       
   NH₃ (μ_net = 1.47 D)             NF₃ (μ_net = 0.23 D)
   Lone Pair (▲)                    Lone Pair (▲)
       │                                │
       N                                N
     / │ \                            / │ \
    H  H  H                          F  F  F
   (▲  ▲  ▲)                        (▼  ▼  ▼)
   Bond dipoles REINFORCE           Bond dipoles OPPOSE
   lone pair moment.                lone pair moment.
conceptBreakdown.content:
• In $\text{NH}_3$, Nitrogen is more electronegative than Hydrogen; the three $\text{N-H}$ bond dipoles point toward Nitrogen, **reinforcing** the lone pair dipole ($\mathbf{\mu = 1.47\text{ D}}$).
• In $\text{NF}_3$, Fluorine is more electronegative than Nitrogen; the three $\text{N-F}$ bond dipoles point away from Nitrogen, **opposing** the lone pair dipole ($\mathbf{\mu = 0.23\text{ D}}$).

• **Percentage Ionic Character (Hannay-Smyth Equation)**:
$$\mathbf{\% \text{ Ionic Character} = 16(\chi_A - \chi_B) + 3.5(\chi_A - \chi_B)^2 = \left( \frac{\mu_{\text{exp}}}{\mu_{\text{ionic}}} \right) \times 100}$$

quickRevision: Symmetrical molecules (CO₂, BF₃, CCl₄, XeF₂, SF₆) have μ_net = 0.
NH₃ (1.47 D) > NF₃ (0.23 D) because bond dipoles reinforce the lone pair in NH₃ but oppose it in NF₃.
